facts.statement: The study used a scoping review design to gather and summarize existing research on how blood pressure fluctuations affect the brain.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: Researchers searched two major medical databases to find studies that looked at how well patients take their blood pressure medication and how stable their blood pressure remains over time.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: The review found that irregular medication use and drugs that wear off quickly are likely linked to greater swings in blood pressure throughout the day.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: Blood pressure variability is connected to brain damage and cognitive issues even when average blood pressure levels are controlled.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors created a new conceptual framework to help doctors better assess individual risks and plan future studies on blood pressure stability.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: The authors conclude that managing hypertension should focus not just on average pressure but also on keeping blood pressure stable over time.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study suggests that monitoring blood pressure stability could be an important addition to current treatments for preventing long-term brain injury.
